chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadda' from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd (1) said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbidding the use of narcissus (nargis), so I said, 'May I be your ransom, for what reason is that?' He said, 'Because it is the scent (rihan) of the foreigners (A'ajim).'
And reports have been narrated regarding the dislike (karahah) of smelling the scent (rihan) as well.

key_terms.الْأَعَاجِمِ: The foreigners (non-Arabs or those distinct from the Ahl al-Bayt's circle)
key_terms.رَيْحَانُ: Scent/fragrance (specifically associated with paradise or general fragrance)
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَةِ: Dislike (a juristic ruling less severe than prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq forbid the use of narcissus?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits the use of narcissus (*nargis*) by identifying it as the distinctive scent of the *A'ajam* (Persians/non-Arabs), reflecting a cultural marker of identity during the Abbasid era. This prohibition is contextualized within broader reports discouraging the consumption of strong scents while fasting, linking sensory pleasure to the potential nullification of spiritual focus or ritual purity.
